hook.text: Twelve people produced 65% of anti-vaccine disinformation on social media. Twelve. Out of billions of users.

buildup.text: The Center for Countering Digital Hate identified the 'Disinformation Dozen' in 2021. They had massive followings.

discovery.text: Network science shows information follows power laws. A few nodes spread most content. Remove them and flow drops.

twist.text: Platforms were slow to act. Some of the twelve still have accounts today. Removing a popular user is a business risk.

climax.text: Superspreaders prove disinfo is concentrated. The problem has identifiable sources—the will to act is what's missing.

punchline.text: A handful of voices can poison a billion feeds.

quiz.question: What did the 'Disinformation Dozen' study reveal?
options: Just 12 people produced most anti-vaccine disinfo
